chunks: Muʿāwiyah ibn Wahb narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said:
"Any judge who judges between two people and errs falls farther than the distance from the heaven."

key_terms.اثْنَيْنِ: two people or two parties in dispute
key_terms.السَّمَاءِ: the heaven, used here as a measure of extreme distance
key_terms.فَأَخْطَأَ: then he erred, meaning he made a wrong judgment
key_terms.قَاضٍ: a judge, one who issues judgment between people
key_terms.قَضَى: he judged or decided a case

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about the danger of a judge making a wrong judgment?
ai.summary: This hadith warns of the grave consequence of error in judging between people. It emphasizes the immense responsibility of judicial authority and the moral danger of issuing an incorrect judgment.
